subject: plot excluding varying missing columns for different ID

messages.author: e4a3215063481170
messages.subject: plot excluding varying missing columns for different ID
parts:
Dear list,

I have a data set with hierarchical structure, that is, measure times nested within IDs. For some ID, some columns are entirely missing, whereas other columns are entirely missing for other ID. I am trying to figure out a code that could plot this situation for all ID, as the data from new ID are keep coming in. Specifically, I would like to get a plot that include all the columns that are not entirely missing. In other words, I don't need the column that is entirely missing, I need the columns with values (although they can have missing values, they are not entirely missing). Ideally, I hope I could get a geom_line() kind of plot that shows the time trend of all columns together in the same plot. 

A replicable code for one group looks like below:

````
df=data.frame(
  id=c(rep(1,3),rep(2,3),rep(3,3),rep(4,3)),
  t=c(rep(c(0,1,2),4)),
  a1=c(rep(NA,3),rep(c(1.3,NA,1.6),3)),
  a2=c(rnorm(3),rep(NA,3),rep(c(1.5,NA,1.2),2)),
  a3=c(rep(c(2.5,NA,3.2),2),rep(NA,3),rnorm(3)),
  a4=rnorm(12)
)
df1=df[df$id==1,]
ggplot(df1)+
  geom_line(data=df1[!is.na(df1$a1),],aes(y=a1,x=t,color='c1'))+geom_point(aes(y=a1,x=t,color='c1'))+
  geom_line(data=df1[!is.na(df1$a2),],aes(y=a2,x=t,color='c2'))+geom_point(aes(y=a2,x=t,color='c2'))+
  geom_line(data=df1[!is.na(df1$a3),],aes(y=a3,x=t,color='c3'))+geom_point(aes(y=a3,x=t,color='c3'))+
  geom_line(data=df1[!is.na(df1$a4),],aes(y=a4,x=t,color='c4'))+geom_point(aes(y=a4,x=t,color='c4'))+
  scale_color_manual(values=c('c1'='red','c2'='yellow','c3'='blue','c4'='green'),labels=c('anx1','anx2','anx3','anx4'))+
  labs(x='time',y='value',title='trend')
````

The error:

````
Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (1): x and y Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.
````

I have intentionally made the data like this.The thing is, the error only shows when ID ==1, 2, 3, but not for ID==4, as the ID==4 dose not have a column that is entirely missing.

Thank you very much.

Best regards,

YA

messages.author: 942ffec526d6a312
messages.subject: Re: plot excluding varying missing columns for different ID
parts:
Hi YA,

You seem to be aware of the problem, so really you
want to avoid a call that doesn't have any plottable
observations. You could do this by replicating your
commands and dropping the relevant geom_line call
for each id level. Or you could use facet_wrap to
produce id-separated graphs, which seems much more
straightforward.

I hope this will be helpful:

```
library(tidyverse)
#
# df is the name of a function, so is best avoided as an object name
DF=data.frame(

#
# Let's make the data long format to avoid all those calls
# to geom_line and use facet_wrap
DFl <- pivot_longer(DF, cols = paste0('a', 1:4))
#
# This should get you started...
gg1 <- ggplot(DFl) +
geom_line(aes(x = t, y = value, colour = name)) +
geom_point(aes(x = t, y = value, colour = name)) +
facet_wrap(~ id, ncol = 2) +
scale_color_manual(values = c('a1' = 'red', 'a2' = 'yellow', 'a3' =
'blue', 'a4' = 'green'),
labels = c('anx1', 'anx2', 'anx3', 'anx4'))+

# or maybe...
gg2 <- DFl %>% filter(!is.na(value)) %>% ggplot(.) +
geom_line(aes(x = t, y = value, colour = name)) +
geom_point(aes(x = t, y = value, colour = name)) +
facet_wrap(~ id, ncol = 2) +
scale_color_manual(values = c('a1' = 'red', 'a2' = 'yellow', 'a3' =
'blue', 'a4' = 'green'),
labels = c('anx1', 'anx2', 'anx3', 'anx4'))+

Then print gg1 or gg2 to see them.

I used geom_point as well as geom_line to show where there
are actual data values. The second version should put a line
where there are two observed data points.

Regards,
Ron.
